newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to brief lawmakers on situation in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to brief lawmakers on situation in Iraq.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will brief top lawmakers on the situation in Iraq on Tuesday morning before leaving on a four-day campaign trip to the Midwest and the West Coast, the White House said on Monday.

Spokeswoman Kathleen McKiernan said Clinton had invited the Republican and Democratic leaders of the House of Representatives and the Senate, as well as the chairs and ranking members of congressional committees and subcommittees to an 8 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT) meeting at the White House.
"We've had consultations continually and this is just another step in this process," McKiernan said.

Clinton has been trying to improve his communications with Congress. He came under fire for not briefing lawmakers before ordering U.S. missile attacks on Iraqi air defenses when Iraqi troops moved into the Kurdish region of northern Iraq.
Administration officials said Tuesday's briefing was not an indication that Washington was planning any major new initiatives in the latest Iraqi crisis.
Both sides have sought to defuse tensions in the past few days, with Clinton telling reporters on Monday, "We have sought no confrontation with (Iraqi President) Saddam Hussein."
But Clinton declined to rule out air strikes against the Gulf state and his top military adviser, U.S. Army General John Shalikashvili, said, "We are not standing down."

The U.S. military buildup continued in the Gulf on Monday and U.S. Defense Secretary William Perry warned the Iraqi leader to stop deploying anti-aircraft missile batteries in the extended southern Iraqi no-fly zone.
Kuwait, the only Middle East country to endorse U.S. missile attacks on Iraq this month, formally approved Washington's plan to send up to 5,000 ground troops to the country bordering Iraq.
